newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila urges troops in Spratlys not to use guns.
newsitem.headline: Manila urges troops in Spratlys not to use guns.

text.p: The Philippines ordered its troops on Wednesday to avoid using guns while driving away Chinese fishing boats from areas it claims in the Spratly islands in an apparent bid to ease diplomatic tension with China.
Instead, Philippine marines occupying eight isles in the disputed South China Sea should use hand signals or radios, armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said.

Philippine troops last weekend fired warning shots at Chinese fishing boats near Kota Island in the Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals which Beijing says historically belongs to China.
The Spratlys are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
"Firing shots to warn fishermen... should not have been the first resort," Acedera told reporters. "When we use firearms for warning people, that could be misinterpreted as provoking."
The incident was the fourth between the two countries in recent weeks.

Manila accused Beijing in April of sending armed ships near two Filipino-occupied islands. Beijing, in turn, protested against the hoisting of the Philippine flag over a rocky outcrop called Scarborough Shoal, well north of the Spratlys.
Manila also angered Beijing last month when a Philippine Navy ship arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near the shoal and filed charges of illegal entry against them.
